Context inputs (`context_inputs: True`, discovered at hash time) are attached to map_compile as well as map_scan. map_compile is the generator whose output (map.json `context`) depends on them. map_scan only reports them, in one CONTEXT summary line.

The payload gets a top-level `context` key, copied from map.json's `context` section through ctxmap.section_from_map, instead of having the template read DATA.map.context. This keeps one degraded shape for the empty project. PayloadEmptyProjectTests gained 3 assertions; none were removed.

Guides inside .claude/ other than the root guide are not discovered, per the DoD's 'outside .claude/'. So for a subtree inside .claude/, --suggest proposes a scoped rule (.claude/rules/<slug>.md, paths <folder>/**) instead of a folder guide. evolution.md says so.

Following the docs page fetched this session (code.claude.com/docs/en/memory), the frontmatter reader also accepts `paths:` as a comma-separated string (split brace-aware), and the glob matcher supports [..] bracket expressions, the \ escape and the 1000-pattern brace budget. Anything YAML would reject is reported as unparseable: an unquoted leading *, unquoted braces in an inline item, tab indents, ': ' in another key's plain value.

SUGGESTIONS: Pre-existing Windows bug in checkctl.check_gitignore_shadowing: it sends `git check-ignore --stdin` input in text mode, so on Windows each query reaches git as 'path\r'. File-level patterns such as *.zip then never match, and only directory patterns (the existing dist/ test) are caught. The fix is the NUL-separated bytes approach used in ctxmap._git_ignored (`-z`, encoded input).

Pre-existing: _lib.sha256_paths hashes absolute path strings, so the generator ledger differs per checkout or machine, and a fresh clone or worktree always reports every generator as 'inputs changed'.
